title: Darth Vader
subtitle: Sith Lord — Original Trilogy
description: Dual-crystal construction with adjustable blade length — a brutally aggressive redesign of his former Jedi weapon, built for Form V power strikes.
designNotes: The hilt retains echoes of Anakin's original but trades elegance for menace — heavier emitter shroud, darker alloy finish, and a grip built for a mechanical hand.

title: Obi-Wan Kenobi
subtitle: Jedi Master — Clone Wars to A New Hope
description: A refined hilt marking Obi-Wan's progression from Padawan to Master. The design moves away from the simpler Qui-Gon-inspired weapon of his youth.
designNotes: The emitter and grip reflect the refined symmetry of Obi-Wan's defensive Soresu style — balanced, compact, and built for endurance over aggression.

title: Mace Windu
subtitle: Jedi Council Senior Member
description: Electrum-plated hilt signifying senior Council status. The rare amethyst blade was produced by a unique kyber crystal.
designNotes: The electrum finish is a status marker — only the most senior Jedi earned this distinction. The hilt geometry is deceptively simple for a weapon of such prestige.

title: Darth Maul
subtitle: Sith Apprentice — The Phantom Menace
description: Iconic double-bladed saber — two connected hilts producing dual blades. Extended reach and intimidating spinning display at the cost of defensive capability.
designNotes: The double-blade form factor is essentially two lightsabers fused end-to-end. The elongated proportions make this the most architecturally distinct weapon in the collection.

title: Rey
subtitle: Jedi — The Rise of Skywalker
description: A scavenger-forged hilt with a rotating activation switch that flashes green and blue before igniting yellow — marking the first of a new Jedi Order.
designNotes: The hilt's salvaged aesthetic is intentional — wrapping and exposed mechanics that honor Rey's resourceful origins while the yellow blade signals something entirely new.

title: Luke Skywalker
subtitle: Jedi Knight — Return of the Jedi
description: Modeled after Obi-Wan's weapon as a tribute, constructed from salvaged materials after losing Anakin's blue saber on Bespin.
designNotes: The clean cylindrical profile and minimal ornamentation reflect Luke's self-taught construction approach — functional, honest, and distinctly his own despite the Obi-Wan influence.

title: Kylo Ren
subtitle: Dark Side — Sequel Trilogy
description: Crossguard design with quillon plasma vents. The unstable, flickering blade was caused by a cracked kyber crystal channeled through lateral vents.
designNotes: The crossguard isn't decorative — it's a structural necessity. The cracked crystal produces excess energy that must be vented laterally, creating the distinctive medieval silhouette.

title: Yoda
subtitle: Grand Master — Prequel Trilogy
description: Compact hilt scaled to Yoda's small stature, yet an elegant and powerful weapon. The simple design belied incredible mastery of ancient lightsaber forms.
designNotes: Proportionally, this is the most compact hilt in the collection. The shorter grip and emitter create a weapon that looks almost ceremonial — until you see it in motion.

title: Count Dooku
subtitle: Sith Lord — Prequel Trilogy
description: The curved hilt was purpose-built for Form II Makashi precision — allowing elegant slashes and lunges with superior dexterity.
designNotes: The curve is the defining feature — an ergonomic choice that optimizes wrist angle for one-handed fencing. Controversial among Jedi, who saw it as prioritizing dueling vanity.

title: Anakin Skywalker
subtitle: Jedi Knight — Episode II
description: Smooth emitter shroud with twin LED indicators — a design later replaced by the more angular Episode III version. Ridged grip optimized for aggressive dueling.
designNotes: Comparing Episode II and III versions reveals Anakin's evolution — the smoother, more refined geometry here gives way to harder angles as he approaches the dark side.

title: Qui-Gon Jinn
subtitle: Jedi Master — The Phantom Menace
description: Alloy-constructed hilt with a subtle curved grip. The green-bladed weapon was built to echo the design language of his former master, Count Dooku.
designNotes: The lineage is visible — Dooku's curve influence is present but restrained. Qui-Gon's version is straighter, more practical, reflecting a master who valued the Living Force over form.

title: Darth Sidious
subtitle: Sith Master — Prequel Trilogy
description: Curved hilt with adjustable blade length and a refined finish — built for Form VII combat against skilled opponents like Yoda and Mace Windu.
designNotes: The most overtly elegant Sith weapon — the refined proportions and precious-metal finish disguise it as an aristocratic accessory, much like Palpatine himself.
